data.title: CBOT wheat futures end lower, notch ninth weekly loss
data.description:
Key points:
  • Black Sea shipments could increase after Russia lets grain export vessels leave Sea of Azov
  • Corn mark fifth weekly loss, soybeans see third weekly decline
  • USDA data show weekly US wheat export sales hit marketing-year high

By P.J. Huffstutter

Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures edged lower on Friday, and set a ninth consecutive weekly loss, as prices remained pressured by prospects of increased Russian wheat exports, and despite strong demand for US grain and reports that China could buy from the US, market analysts said.

Corn futures also fell, with the most-active contract notching a fifth consecutive weekly loss on growing US harvest supplies and fund liquidation as traders adjusted positions ahead of month end, analysts said.

While CBOT soybeans ended the day mixed on bargain-buying and signs of export demand, with deferred months ending lower. While the most-active contract was up for much of the session, it eased late in the day and marked a third straight weekly loss.

Exporters sold 165,150 metric tons of US soybeans received in the reporting period to unknown destinations for 2026/27 delivery, the US Department of Agriculture said in its daily reporting system on Friday. USDA also reported that an additional 132,000 tons of US soybeans were sold to unknown destinations for the 2026/2027 marketing year.

The most-traded wheat contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) settled down 1/4 cent at $6.03-1/2 per bushel. Prices fell to $5.93-1/4 on Wednesday, the lowest since July 1, and the contract has fallen more than 23% over the past nine weeks.

"The funds are setting record short positions in the wheat market, and we're taking ever-more risk premium in that market," said Don Roose of U.S. Commodities in West Des Moines, Iowa.

CBOT corn settled down 3-1/2 cents at $4.47-3/4 per bushel, as the contract has fallen about 15% over the past five weeks. CBOT soybeans closed down 1/2 cent at $12.34-1/4 a bushel.

Shipments from the Black Sea could increase after sources said Russia, the world's largest wheat exporter, had allowed grain export vessels to leave the Sea of Azov for the first time since July 10.

However, attacks continue in the region, with a Greek container ship sunk on Thursday. On the demand side, Bloomberg reported on Thursday that buyers in China, the world's biggest crop importer, were seeking offers on US soft red winter wheat.

US exports were already running above expectations, with USDA data showing net export sales of 2026-27 wheat in the week to October 22 at 849,800 metric tons, a marketing-year high.

But traders have also been keeping a close eye on both geopolitical stress and investor positioning ahead of next week's US election, said market analysts.

US President Donald Trump, ​speaking ahead of ‌November 3 midterm congressional elections, said on ​Friday he ​believed the war with ⁠Iran will end ​soon, without saying when.

Previous statements from the White House indicating that military action will take place against Iran following the election are "causing managed money to leak out of the market, especially the commodities," Karl Setzer, partner at Consus Ag, said in an analyst note.

data.title: Wall Street analysts call the Binance hack selloff a buying opportunity for crypto stocks
data.description:
Crypto just suffered the largest theft in its history. Wall Street's response was to tell clients to go shopping.

Analysts at Cantor Fitzgerald, TD Cowen and Compass Point are framing the recent Binance breach as a dip worth buying in crypto-linked equities rather than a signal to exit. Their argument is that the hack is unlikely to throw the broader market's recovery off course or to threaten the solvency of the exchange itself.

The breach unfolded on October 29-30, 2026. Attackers drained approximately $6.3 billion from Binance hot wallets spread across ten blockchains.

The whole operation reportedly took somewhere between 20 and 30 minutes.

A hot wallet is the exchange's cash register: it stays connected to the internet so withdrawals can be processed quickly. Cold wallets are the vault in the back, kept offline.

The entry point traced back to a compromised laptop belonging to a Binance DevOps engineer. That access let the attackers reach a service container used to handle withdrawals.

Blockchain analytics firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis have attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a group associated with North Korea. The research points to a sophisticated operation that exploited Ethereum features and worked to wipe away digital traces of the intrusion.

Crypto-linked stocks sold off hard as news of the breach spread. Coinbase, Robinhood and MicroStrategy all saw immediate declines as investors reacted to the headline number.

The analyst case for calm rests on three pillars. The first is recovery. Analysts point out that roughly $3 billion of the affected assets has already been frozen through coordination with stablecoin issuers including Tether and Circle.

The second pillar is Binance's balance sheet. The exchange has pledged to make customers whole using company reserves exceeding $6.34 billion, a figure that includes $5 billion held in matching tokens.

The third is operational containment. Binance paused withdrawals as a precaution and expects to restart them within days. Deposits stayed open throughout, and the exchange has said user funds are safe.

Taken together, the analysts' reading is that Binance has enough liquidity to absorb the hit. In their view, the selloff in names like Coinbase and Robinhood priced in a systemic crisis that the facts do not currently support.

Not everyone is reaching for the buy button. Moody's took a more measured stance, highlighting the risks that come with hot wallets and with concentrating large amounts of value in a single venue.

The ratings agency also placed the incident against the backdrop of a long history of North Korean cyberattacks on the sector.

The Binance theft surpasses the previous record set by the Bybit hack in 2025.

For equity investors, the analyst thesis is essentially a bet on contagion staying contained. Coinbase and Robinhood did not lose customer funds here.

That bet depends on a few things holding up. Binance needs to resume withdrawals on the timeline it has signaled. The frozen $3 billion needs to stay frozen. And the reserve pledge needs to translate into customers actually seeing their balances restored.

MicroStrategy is a slightly different case. Its shares trade largely as a proxy for crypto prices, so its path depends more on whether the hack drags on broader digital-asset sentiment than on anything Binance does operationally.

A single compromised engineer laptop opening a route to withdrawal infrastructure is the kind of detail that tends to show up in compliance reviews and regulator questions. Moody's emphasis on hot-wallet and concentration risk hints at where that scrutiny is likely to land.

The stablecoin angle deserves attention too. The ability of Tether and Circle to freeze a large share of the stolen funds turned centralized controls into a recovery tool.

data.title: Fast-Fashion Billionaire Pays $31 Million for New York Penthouse — WSJ
data.description:
By Katherine Clarke

Richard Saghian, the chief executive of fast-fashion giant Fashion Nova, already has palatial homes in Los Angeles and Miami Beach, Fla. Now, he's making a bet on New York.

Saghian's real-estate agent, Ryan Serhant of Serhant, confirmed that the billionaire paid $31 million for a penthouse at the Tribeca condominium 111 Murray Street. The five-bedroom apartment measures about 7,700 square feet with views of the Hudson and East Rivers.

The deal brings the building, which launched preconstruction sales in the summer of 2015, to 100% sold, according to a spokesperson for Douglas Elliman Development Marketing, whose agent Emily Sertic led sales at the tower.

Saghian's unit has a fireplace and a roughly 1,400-square-foot primary suite with two dressing rooms. Amenities at the building, which is about 800 feet tall, include a Turkish bath, a private dining room, a 75-foot lap pool, a fitness center and an arcade for teens.

Saghian started Fashion Nova in 2006. The company made its name by offering new clothing styles every week, and was promoted on social media by influencers and celebrities. As Saghian's wealth has grown, he has assembled a portfolio of luxury homes. Most notably, he paid $126 million in 2022 for a 105,000-square-foot megamansion in Los Angeles called the One. He also owns property on tony North Bay Road in Miami Beach.

For Manhattan properties priced at or over $4 million, contract activity rose by 2.5% in September from the same month of 2025, according to a recent Elliman report.

Serhant worked on the Saghian deal with his wife, Emilia Serhant.

data.title: The Week the Cracks in the AI Trade Grew Deeper — WSJ
data.description:
By David Uberti and Hannah Erin Lang

Slowing growth. Dwindling cash piles. Cannibalized business lines. Pressure points are multiplying across the artificial-intelligence boom that has propelled markets and the economy.

The cracks in the AI trade multiplied through the week, culminating in a sharp tech selloff Friday that sent the Nasdaq composite to its worst day since June and its worst month in more than a year.

The vulnerabilities in Wall Street's favorite trade have been building for months, periodically appearing around smaller companies drowning in debt. Each time, the largest firms behind America's AI build-out have reassured Wall Street by printing profits, suggesting the show will go on even in a world of higher interest rates.

This week was different. After tech stocks had treaded water for weeks, AI giant Anthropic momentarily rejuvenated investors with a filing that showed soaring revenue ahead of its planned initial public offering. But then publicly traded tech firms reported earnings — and markets got a reality check.

First came a dissatisfying quarterly report from Alphabet, which showed that growth in Google's search-advertising business slowed — in part because of the impact of "AI mode" queries. Traders punished the stock with a 13% decline Thursday that marked its worst day on record, hammering major Alphabet shareholders such as Berkshire Hathaway.

Then the bad tech vibes got worse. Late Thursday, Amazon reported plunging free cash flow and revenue that missed analyst estimates. American chipmaking giant Intel forecast a prolonged slowdown in personal-computer sales, pressured by memory chip prices sent skyrocketing by the AI boom.

Intel shares on Friday crashed about 30%, the worst session on record for a company that has traded on the U.S. stock market for decades. The plunge vaporized more than $15 billion in combined paper holdings by two of the company's largest shareholders: the U.S. government and Nvidia.

Write to David Uberti at david.uberti@wsj.com and Hannah Erin Lang at hannaherin.lang@wsj.com

OTTAWA--Canada declared as a national priority a proposed expansion at the country's busiest port in Vancouver, British Columbia, arguing that it is required for the country to meet its goal of doubling non-U.S. exports by 2035.

The designation also kicks off an accelerated regulatory review process, whereby officials are tasked with determining how the expansion proceeds and under what conditions, as opposed to whether it requires approval.

Officials said this puts the timing for a final investment decision from the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority by mid-2027.

"We cannot afford to let bottlenecks hold back Canadian trade," Canadian Transport Minister Steven MacKinnon said Friday at a press conference in suburban Vancouver. "The sooner we build the [trade] capacity Canada needs, the sooner Canadian businesses and workers can benefit."

The authority, which manages the Vancouver port, said the expansion project would increase container capacity by about 50%, through a new land-mass and wharf structure covering 300 acres. This additional capacity could support annual trade of 100 billion Canadian dollars (US$71.5 billion).

Officials peg the project's cost at C$5.9 billion. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has pledged up to C$10 billion in financial support for Pacific coast trade corridors.

The port authority said the Vancouver terminal currently handles more than C$1 billion in commerce daily, and more cargo than the next five largest Canadian ports combined.

The expansion, upgrade and construction of trade corridors across Canada is a priority initiative for Carney, who has argued that it is necessary to restore resilience in the economy and reduce the country's reliance on U.S. trade to drive economic growth.

According to government documents, there needs to be a "significant expansion" of Canada's port capacity to diversify trade, adding that 80% of trade with non-U.S. markets is done by sea. The prime minister has set a goal of doubling the level of non-U.S. exports by 2035.

"Continued inaction on port expansion could eventually force Canadian importers and exporters to utilize U.S. ports--a dependency that is untenable in the current geopolitical circumstances," officials said, according to documents distributed at a technical briefing. "Port expansion is thus integral to ensuring Canadian sovereignty and control over key economic linkages to the rest of the world," the officials said, according to the documents.

Officials warned that without port expansion, Canada could face sharply higher shipping costs of up to C$900 million a year due to traffic congestion and insufficient capacity.

Bank of Canada researchers warned this year that the country lacked the port capacity to executive the government's trade agenda.

The central bank's analysis indicated Canadian ports can't accommodate some of the latest ultra-large container ships being deployed. Because of this, some goods originating from China and destined for Canada and loaded onto these big vessels have to dock in Los Angeles--and those goods could be subject to U.S. tariffs.

Write to Paul Vieira at paul.vieira@wsj.com

data.title: Southern Copper 2026: Revenue $4.7B, EPS $2.15— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Southern Copper reported 2026 results with revenue of $4.7B and net income of $1.8B, up 39.1% and 62.7%, respectively, from the prior-year period. Diluted EPS rose 62.9% to $2.15, with higher metal prices supporting sales despite lower copper sales volume.

Financial Highlights

MetricCurrent quarterPrior year quarterYoY change
Revenue¹$4.7B$3.38B39.1%
Net income²$1.8B$1.11B62.7%
Diluted EPS³$2.15$1.3262.9%

¹ Reported as “Net sales (including sales to related parties, see note 5)”. ² Reported as “Net income attributable to SCC”. ³ Reported as “Per common share amounts attributable to SCC”.

Business Highlights

  • Net sales rose 39.1%, driven by higher copper, molybdenum, silver and zinc prices despite lower copper sales volume.
  • Refined copper, including SX-EW, accounted for 55.8% of Q3 copper sales, compared with 40.5% a year earlier; concentrate sales declined to 27.7% from 42.4%.
  • Mined copper production fell 1.1% in Q3 and 2.9% over the first nine months, as gains at Buenavista were partly offset by lower output at Peruvian mines.
  • By-product credits helped reduce net cash cost to $0.09 per pound from $0.42, while by-product revenue per pound increased 30.6%.
  • Southern Copper forecast 2026 copper output of 918,000 tonnes. Tia Maria was 49.6% complete, with first production targeted for the first half of 2028.

Original SEC Filing: SOUTHERN COPPER CORP/ [ SCCO ] - 10-Q - Oct. 30, 2026

data.title: Consumer Portfolio Services 3Q 2026: Revenue $131.9M, Net income $7M, EPS $0.3— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Consumer Portfolio Services, Inc. reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $131.9M, up 21.7% from $108.4M a year earlier, and net income of $7M, compared with $4.9M. Diluted EPS rose to $0.3 from $0.2, as higher interest income reflected growth in the average receivables balance.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $131.9M, compared with $108.4M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 21.7%.
  • Net income was $7.0M, compared with $4.9M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 43.3%.
  • Diluted EPS was $0.30, compared with $0.20 in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 50.0%.

Business Highlights

  • Nine-month revenue increased 12.5% to $365.6M, while contract purchases reached $2.1B, up from $1.3B a year earlier. Third-quarter purchases more than doubled year over year.
  • The managed portfolio grew to $4.84B at September 30, 2026, from $3.90B a year earlier.
  • Sales staff increased to 167 from 116, supporting higher originations, while total employees rose to 1,010 from 918.
  • Annualized net charge-offs improved to 7.26% from 8.01% year over year; delinquencies increased to 10.90% from 10.20%.

Original SEC Filing: CONSUMER PORTFOLIO SERVICES, INC. [ CPSS ] - 10-Q - Oct. 30, 2026
